Original synthetic AVIF fixtures, MIT OR Apache-2.0, created 2026-10-25.
No external artwork is included.

generate.py uses FFmpeg/libaom to encode rgb-lossless.avif: an 8x6 RGB grid
with red in columns 0..2, green in the upper-right and blue in the lower-right.
It uses AV1 RGB identity coding at CRF 0. Decoder output matches every pixel.
rotated.avif, mirrored.avif and rotated-mirrored.avif add associated irot/imir
properties, adjust enclosing box sizes and relocate the single coded extent.
They test anticlockwise rotation, horizontal reflection, and rotation followed
by vertical reflection. These property mutations are synthetic reader fixtures.

oversized-width.avif is a 17000x1 black image, generated by the same script.
oversized-area.avif is a 4098x4098 black image from:
    ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=black:size=4098x4098 -frames:v 1 \
        -c:v libaom-av1 -cpu-used 8 -crf 40 oversized-area.avif
The native preflight frame-size limit rejects its 16,793,604 pixels.
hdr-declaration.avif uses YUV444 BT.2020 matrix coding; the script deliberately
sets container NCLX primaries 9 and transfer 16 to test explicit HDR rejection.
Its synthetic pixel values are not an HDR reference rendering.

rgba-export.avif is the original 4x3 RGBA grid in ../jxl/rgba-lossless.jxl,
exported with examples/raster_export.rs at quality 90. rgba-export.rgba stores
independent FFmpeg/libaom decoded RGB (stream 0) plus grayscale alpha (stream 1).
Import is compared against all 48 bytes. Source colors may change during lossy
encoding and hidden RGB may be discarded; the preview reflects decoded output.

linear-icc.avif contains the two RGB pixels from examples/linear_profile_probe.rs,
encoded by FFmpeg/libaom at CRF 0, gbrp/full range. The PNG's decompressed iCCP
profile was attached as an associated colr/prof property using generate.py's
transform_properties helper. Alpha was deliberately omitted by this fixture's
RGB encoding. The first stored gray pixel is 128; sRGB conversion yields 188.

FFmpeg version and system codec builds are host-provided. These fixture files
are fixed test inputs; byte-for-byte encoder reproducibility is not assumed.
